rows.label: Share of Earthjustice's programme spending on climate and clean energy

source.title: Earthjustice, Financial Statements, June 30, 2025 and 2024 (BPM LLP, auditors)
source.quote: Earthjustice has two programs, Litigation and Public Information, with key focus areas of: advancing clean energy and a stable climate

rows.explainer: Our judgment, read by charityevals' three Earthjustice models so the split is one set of numbers: the audited accounts split programmes only into litigation and public information, across three focus areas (clean energy and climate; healthy communities, keeping toxics out of air and water; and the wild, species and ecosystems). Anchor: climate and clean energy holds the most of its programme teams (Clean Energy, Fossil Fuels, much of International) and of its state work (more than 130 utility-commission and other matters in 18 states beyond New York and California in fiscal 2025, Annual Report p. 24), and the largest part of the fiscal 2025 annual report. 45% (35% to 55%).

rows.label: Share of Earthjustice's programme spending on healthy communities (toxics in air and water)

source.title: Earthjustice, Financial Statements, June 30, 2025 and 2024 (BPM LLP, auditors)
source.quote: safeguarding healthy communities by keeping toxics out of our air and water

rows.explainer: Our judgment (see climate_share): the Toxic Exposure and Health, Sustainable Food and Farming and Community Partnerships programmes and the regional offices' air and water cases (national air standards, chemical plants, refineries, drinking water, pesticides, coal ash). 25% (15% to 35%). Biodiversity takes the rest (biodiversity_share).

rows.label: Share of Earthjustice's programme spending on biodiversity (species, lands and oceans)

source.title: Earthjustice, Financial Statements, June 30, 2025 and 2024 (BPM LLP, auditors)
source.quote: preserving the wild by protecting endangered species and the ecosystems that sustain them

rows.explainer: Our judgment (see climate_share): the Biodiversity Defense, Oceans and Tribal Partnerships programmes and the regional offices' public-lands, forest and wildlife cases (the Endangered Species Act, the Roadless Rule, national monuments). 30% (20% to 40%). The three shares are set to sum to 100% at their best guesses; each model reads its own.
